description:
An ordinary carton can reveal a much bigger supply problem. Egg prices in America can climb when bird flu disrupts production, and rebuilding laying flocks takes time. This short explainer follows the pressure from poultry farms to the supermarket shelf, covering lost egg production, feed and transportation costs, and demand that does not disappear when supplies tighten. It also explains why cage-free and conventional cartons can carry different prices, and why your local shelf price may not immediately reflect changes further up the supply chain. What are you paying for a dozen eggs in your city? Share the price and carton type in the comments
